additional_findings.title: Late Finance invoice posting subtracts Sales payments twice
additional_findings.reproduction: Invoice 147500, allocated receipt 50000, then Finance invoice/receipt/allocation import produced bill outstanding 47500 while Sales and the general ledger showed 97500. Fully paid invoices could reject allocation import.
additional_findings.fix: New Finance invoice bill references start at the gross posted invoice amount; imported receipt allocations reduce them exactly once. Existing mapped bills retain their stored balances.
additional_findings.evidence: Four integrated API cases cover partial/full collection with Finance import before/after Sales payment, payment requests without money movement, invoice/receipt/allocation posting, general ledger and report reconciliation, and idempotent retries. Nine Finance posting/order-to-cash checks pass.
additional_findings.limitations: Historical live bill balances have not been audited or rewritten.

additional_findings.title: Cross-year leave charges only the starting year allowance
additional_findings.reproduction: A Dec 31-Jan 1 request with one day allocated in each year was rejected as needing two days from the first year. A missing next-year allocation could be bypassed when the first year had enough days.
additional_findings.fix: Validate every annual segment before writing, reserve each year separately, and use recorded pending ledger debits for approval/rejection/cancellation. Historical requests retain their original charged year, including ledger entries without a linked balance ID.
additional_findings.evidence: 21 leave/balance checks pass, including six new API cases for annual decisions, no partial writes when next-year allowance is missing, and linked/unlinked historical ledger compatibility.
additional_findings.limitations: No live balances were rewritten; production HRMS read failures remain unverified.

additional_findings.title: Zero approvals are replaced by requested amounts in payroll
additional_findings.reproduction: An expense claim for 2500 with finance-approved amount 0 became a 2500 payroll reimbursement. A salary advance requested for 2500 and reviewed with approval 0 was also recorded as 2500, and recovery calculation treated zero as missing.
additional_findings.fix: Use a null check rather than truthiness in expense linking, advance review and payroll recovery. Preserve explicit zero/partial approvals and legacy null fallbacks. Negative and over-request advance approvals are rejected before writes.
additional_findings.evidence: 10 focused tests and 6 real-world payroll tests pass, including actual payroll calculation/recovery components for zero/partial/null approvals, invalid review without state changes, reimbursement link idempotency, proration, attendance rules, department scope and locked-run protection.
additional_findings.limitations: No live payroll, payment transfer or historical record repair was performed.

additional_findings.title: Reviewed and recovered salary advances can be changed again
additional_findings.reproduction: After payroll marked an advance Recovered and linked it to a payroll record, a new review request changed its approved amount, status and review metadata. The existing UI also left review buttons enabled for these rows.
additional_findings.fix: Lock the advance during review and permit a decision only while it is pending and not linked to payroll. Disable UI actions for reviewed/recovered/linked rows, in-flight mutations and missing approval access. Approval failures show the server reason and refresh stale rows.
additional_findings.evidence: Nine backend checks pass, including actual payroll recovery with zero/partial/null approvals, unchanged recovered records after rejected repeat requests, one-time approved/rejected decisions and retained one-time inputs on payroll reruns. Fourteen phone/desktop UI cases and TypeScript pass.
additional_findings.limitations: No historical payroll rows were rewritten or live salary-advance reviews performed.

additional_findings.title: Foreign expenses are copied into INR payroll without conversion
additional_findings.reproduction: A USD 10.01 finance-approved claim created an INR 10.01 reimbursement, and missing exchange rates did not block linking.
additional_findings.fix: Convert foreign claims to INR using the existing payroll period-start exchange-rate policy and money rounding. Validate all needed rates before any reimbursement writes, reject missing/nonpositive rates, preserve original claims, and record source amount/currency/rate/effective date in reimbursement descriptions. Existing linked claims remain untouched.
additional_findings.evidence: Seven isolated API/payroll checks pass: original INR approval/idempotency, zero/null approvals, foreign conversion at the latest valid period-start rate, ignored future rate, no partial writes when a rate is missing, duplicate retry safety and existing multi-currency payroll behavior.
additional_findings.limitations: Historical reimbursements were not recalculated. Live payroll and expense workflows remain pending.

additional_findings.title: Expense linking ignores payroll department and employee-category scopes
additional_findings.reproduction: A department-specific payroll run considered an unrelated employee claim in the same branch. INR claims could link to the wrong run; an unrelated USD claim without a rate blocked the selected department.
additional_findings.fix: Apply the existing payroll employee-scope query to claims before currency validation or reimbursement creation, preserving company, branch, department, pay-group branch and category semantics used by payroll.
additional_findings.evidence: Ten checks pass after this fix: four department/category cases with excluded INR/USD claims, five existing and currency-aware expense-link checks, and the real payroll department-scoping test. Excluded claims remain unlinked and do not require exchange rates.
additional_findings.limitations: Historical mislinked claims were not rewritten; live workflow retests remain pending.

additional_findings.title: Expense claims can be linked into locked or paid payroll
additional_findings.reproduction: Linking a finance-approved expense to a locked run returned success and created an approved reimbursement plus claim links.
additional_findings.fix: Apply the existing scoped locked-period guard before reading claims or creating reimbursements. Canonical and legacy locked/paid statuses are protected.
additional_findings.evidence: Fourteen isolated API/calculation checks pass: four locked/paid and legacy-status no-write cases, original expense and FX handling, department/category exclusions and the real payroll lock workflow.
additional_findings.limitations: No historical payroll inputs or live records were rewritten.

additional_findings.title: Reimbursement review can rewrite inputs already consumed by payroll
additional_findings.reproduction: After payroll calculation marked a reimbursement Paid and linked it to a payroll record, reviewing it again returned success and changed its status to Approved. This breaks the consumed-input selection used for payroll reruns.
additional_findings.fix: Lock the reimbursement during review; reject reviews of rows linked to payroll or marked Paid. Apply the existing locked-period guard to unconsumed reviews as well. Rejected requests do not change status, reviewer, linkage or ledger.
additional_findings.evidence: Eight checks pass across two focused runs: actual payroll consumption, rejected approve/reject attempts with preserved metadata and ledger, unchanged recalculated payroll, unconsumed reviews blocked in a locked period, retained reimbursement/advance/overtime/encashment inputs on reruns, and valid pending approval/rejection with submission and decision ledger entries.
additional_findings.limitations: No historical consumed inputs were repaired or real payments made; live workflows remain unverified.

additional_findings.fix: Validate required company business defaults in CompanyCreate/CompanyUpdate, shared by legacy create/edit and the settings profile adapter: known timezone, uppercase three-letter currency, fiscal month 1-12 and working days 1-7. Reject null/blank invalid defaults before writes while preserving omitted fields in partial updates. Response schemas remain compatible with historical records.

One additional selected-branch create/edit/readback/reassignment-rejection check passes separately. No live company configuration was modified.

additional_findings.title: Branch settings retain old-company branch, member and ownership data
additional_findings.reproduction: A company/branch switch during rename left the previous branch, member email, unassigned customer ownership record and busy rename modal visible; the new company branch did not load. The branch-family queries lacked company/branch context keys.
additional_findings.fix: Key the branch settings family by record scope; scope branch, lifecycle, membership and ownership queries and cancel obsolete reads. Guard mutations and completion effects with active context ownership. Reset pending action state on switches. Refresh the authoritative version after a rename conflict while retaining the typed name/reason. Completed branch writes refresh in background; creation fields are disabled while submitting.
additional_findings.evidence: Phone/desktop branch rename tests pass for stale-version recovery with the refreshed expected_version, retained draft, scoped branch/member/ownership caches, pending-modal reset, suppression of old completion refresh/messages and read-only controls. Existing branch creation failure/retry/closure/reset and aggregate selector pass at 390/1440 pixels through a self-contained Vite runner. Six isolated lifecycle-service tests pass for data/grant retention, stale-version and restricted-scope rejection, last-active protection and valid recovery. TypeScript passes.
additional_findings.limitations: Mocked browser APIs and isolated SQLite service tests; complete membership/ownership write matrices, remaining lifecycle UI actions and live retests remain pending.
